newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium, zinc to shine as metals rise - ED&F Man.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium, zinc to shine as metals rise - ED&F Man.

text.p: Prices of most base metals, especially zinc and aluminium, are set to push higher as stronger world economic growth and improved fundamentals boost markets, broker E.D. and F. Man said in a report.
"The base metals have rebounded from the late 1996 lows and appear poised to move higher, not unlike the bull market of 1994," Man said.

"The common threads among the base metals include an improving global economy, a shift from consumer destocking to restocking, a slowdown in primary production growth, an improved East West trade balance, and generally low or declining inventories," it added.
Industrial production is expected to rise to 3.0-3.5 percent this year after 2.0 percent in 1996.

"Although at the moment base metals prices are over-extended on the upside...the outlook for 1997 and early 1998 generally calls for higher prices, particularly for zinc and aluminium," the broker said.
Only copper has a less rosy outlook and may see lower prices, if not in the second half of 1997, then by the second half of the following year.
Deficit markets are expected in the first halves of 1997 and 1998 but larger inventory builds are likely in the second halves of each year.
"For 1997 stocks are expected to rise 130,000 tonnes and increase another 170,000 tonnes in 1998," Man said.
Prices, basis spot Comex, are expected to average 108.8 cents per lb in 1997 and 97.5 cents/lb the following year.
In aluminium, the supply-demand deficit is forecast at 380,000 tonnes in 1997 and the stocks-consumption ratio slipping to "a somewhat tight" 7.5 weeks.
Prices, basis LME cash, are seen averaging $1,681 per tonne this year and $1,763 in 1998.
Zinc stocks are seen declining by 200,000 tonnes in 1997 and 100,000 tonnes the following year, trimming the stocks-consumption ratio to five weeks.
Cash zinc is expected to average $1,113 per tonne in 1997 and $1,244 in 1998.
